cohort: The study included 12,045 singleton term pregnancies from Saudi Arabia.
finding: The study found that macrosomia prevalence among Saudi women is 3.4% (>4kg) and is associated with increased maternal age, parity, gestational age, hyperglycemia, and pre-pregnancy obesity, leading to higher risks of shoulder dystocia, emergency cesarean section, stillbirth, and low APGAR scores.
mod_finding: Delivering a macrosomic baby, regardless of the definition used, was associated with an increased risk of emergency cesarean section.
birth_weight: All singleton term births, with macrosomia defined as >4 kg or >=3.7 kg (90th percentile).
